overall: As of approximately 06:45 PT, Los Angeles is sitting under a marine layer with patchy fog and a flat temperature trend — the running max of 66.2°F was established early this morning and current temps have actually dipped slightly to 64.4°F with zero warming velocity. High dewpoints (60.8°F) and SSW flow confirm strong onshore marine influence that is suppressing solar heating, and the day is running cooler than most NWP models anticipated.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are meaningfully split: GFS (78.2°F) and ECMWF (77.3°F) run 3–6°F warmer than NBM (71.8°F) and the official NWS forecast (75°F), while HRRR (75.6°F) sits in between. The marine layer persistence and the flat observed trend this morning lend more credibility to the NBM/NWS lower end, as GFS and ECMWF may be underestimating the marine layer's staying power.
max_temp_prediction: Today's high is most likely to land in the 73–75°F range once the marine layer erodes mid-morning and afternoon sea-breeze kicks in, but robust warming beyond 75°F seems unlikely given the sustained high dewpoints and zero velocity trend. The active even-bucket Kalshi market strongly favors the 72–73°F bucket (61.6%), which is plausible if the marine layer lingers into early afternoon; however, NWS and HRRR both support a push toward 74–75°F if clearing arrives on schedule around 11am. Moderate confidence, leaning toward the lower 74°F range with downside risk toward 72–73°F.
